Twenty-one selected new public filings (718 pages) fully OCR-screened at 150 dpi with RapidOCR and DirectML: Magnien 5/182, Saint Roch 2/62, Saint Loup 3/121, Chezeaux 4/108, Grains de Lune 4/165, Le Clos Saint Denis 3/80. Selection is bounded, not every deposited filing.

Reused Bertagna 5/72, Dujac 4/140, Georges Lignier 3/173 and Arlaud 1/55 research and effort. The separately dated 1990 deed is in the already-screened Lignier PDF; neither it nor the unresolved Lignier U-id duplicates screening counts.

Saint Roch U21940937 is crosswalked through company records and three exact schedules. U21585571 remains unresolved: SIREN 429825250 already has separate rights in this cru and cannot be assigned from a matching name. No current producer is inferred from Jouan, Magnien or Lignier relatives/shareholders.

Saint Loup recites a Jean Paul Magnien lease ending September 2019. Saint Roch prints an 18-year lease effective January 2004 but ending December 2022; the inconsistent duration/dates are retained, and no renewal is presumed. The Arlaud and Dujac original leases and current renewals remain unreviewed.

The Magnien deed is dated 18 December 1998, deposited in a composite 2005 filing. It transfers plantations/business assets, expressly excludes underlying land and describes only 310 m2 of AB472 as Grand Cru. Historical operation context is retained with explicit user approval; adjudication under #364 and current operation remain separate.

Four supplied Winehog texts were reviewed. Attached common maps add context but some lazy-loaded producer maps are absent. Text supplies all accepted numbers/areas; CLF AB403 has an area mismatch. No map-only allocation or correction is made.

Unsupplied paywalled Winehog: Clos Saint-Denis overview (2015-08-30, https://winehog.org/vineyard-insight-clos-saint-denis-the-queen-of-morey-24456/); Domaine Arlaud (2024-09-24, https://winehog.org/terroir-insight-domaine-arlaud-clos-saint-denis-2-33130/); Domaine Dujac (2017-08-23, https://winehog.org/terroir-insight-domaine-dujac-clos-saint-denis-32844/). Only available public text is used; no login or paywall bypass.

The public 2025 Chezeaux article distinguishes the new estate from Hudelot-Noellat. The supplied 2024 Ponsot article leaves recent operator years uncertain. Neither article assigns a current tenant to AB246/255.

Former AP26 reaches AP232/AP233 through existing official DFI ancestry, without current ownership allocation. Other unmatched old references remain unresolved. Original property/lease instruments, paid SPF copies and present-season confirmation remain gaps.
